papers.abstract_original: Background : Vector-borne diseases (VBDs) are an evolving public health concern in Switzerland, where endemic tick-borne infections coexist with emerging mosquito-borne threats linked to climate and ecological change. Public preparedness depends on population knowledge, risk perception, and preventive behaviour alongside institutional capacity. We assessed knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) regarding VBDs among adults in the canton of Bern, interpreted alongside a complementary national stakeholder survey. Methods : We analysed a 2025 cross-sectional web-based survey embedded in the BEready cohort. After validity screening, we derived a latent knowledge score using a two-parameter logistic item response theory (IRT) model fitted to knowledge items. Multivariable linear regression examined associations between participant characteristics and latent knowledge. We identified KAP profiles through partitioning-around-medoids clustering based on block-weighted Gower dissimilarities. A parallel survey of cantonal and Liechtenstein authorities in human health, animal health, and environment departments provided institutional context. Results : Among 1,847 respondents, 1,337 met validity criteria. Knowledge was strongest for tick-related content: 98% matched tick-borne encephalitis to ticks, 87% did so for Lyme disease. Mosquito-borne knowledge was markedly weaker, with only 36% correctly classifying chikungunya and 43% West Nile fever as mosquito-borne, despite 53 % reporting at least weekly summer mosquito exposure. Tick checks were reported by 79% of participants versus 30% for mosquito standing-water removal. The IRT model indicated that mosquito-borne items were both hardest and most discriminating. Higher knowledge was associated with educational attainment, female sex, residence history, tick-bite frequency, and travel history, alongside a non-linear age effect peaking in mid-adulthood. Clustering identified six KAP profiles distinguishing knowledge gaps, low perceived relevance, and weak translation of knowledge into practice. The stakeholder survey (n=55) showed institutional engagement was considerably more developed for mosquito-borne than tick-borne diseases, although about half of authorities reported no dedicated human resources (49%) or budget (55%). Conclusion : Public knowledge and practice remain stronger for tick-borne than mosquito-borne diseases, despite frequent mosquito exposure, revealing a communication gap. Institutional preparedness shows the opposite pattern, being more developed for mosquito-borne threats. Public health strategies should sustain effective tick-prevention messaging while strengthening mosquito-borne disease communication, household source reduction, and support for community-level surveillance and control.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 由于地方性蜱传感染以及气候和生态变化带来的新出现的蚊媒风险,媒介 传播疾病 (VBD) 对瑞士的公共卫生构成了不断变化的威胁。该研究旨在评估人群有关 VBD 的知识、态度和实践 (KAP),为公共卫生做好准备提供信息。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 瑞士伯尔尼州 2025 年 BEready 队列研究 中嵌入了一项基于网络的横断面调查,并辅之以对州和列支敦士登当局在人类健康、动物健康和环境部门进行的平行调查。
elements_zh.methods: 对调查响应进行有效性筛选,并使用双参数逻辑项目响应理论 (IRT) 模型得出潜在知识得分。多变量线性回归评估了参与者特征和知识得分之间的关​​联,而 KAP 概况则通过基于块加权高尔差异的围绕中心点聚类进行分区来确定。
elements_zh.main_results: 在 1,847 名受访者中,1,337 人符合有效性标准,其中 98% 的人正确地将蜱传脑炎与蜱虫联系起来,87% 的人正确地将蜱传脑炎与莱姆病联系起来,而只有 36% 的人将基孔肯雅热和 43% 的西尼罗热视为蚊媒疾病,尽管 53% 的人报告经常接触蚊子。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究强调,尽管接触蚊子传播疾病的人数较多,但在蚊媒疾病方面仍存在明显的知识差距,揭示了将意识转化为预防实践方面的沟通失败。研究发现,针对蚊媒威胁的机构准备比针对蜱传疾病的准备更为完善。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 维持有效的蜱虫预防信息传递,同时加强蚊媒疾病沟通和减少家庭源头至关重要,同时支持社区级 监测 和控制措施,以弥补已发现的差距。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 横截面设计限制了因果推断,并且研究重点关注单个州可能会降低普遍性;然而,使用经过验证的 IRT 建模和聚类增强了研究结果的内部有效性。

papers.title: MoS2/carbon nanotubes nanocomposite thin films as platform for electrochemical dengue detection.
papers.abstract: Sensitive electrochemical immunosensors are important for addressing global health challenges, particularly for the rapid and affordable diagnosis of infectious diseases such as dengue fever. This work reports the preparation and characterization of molybdenum disulphide/carbon nanotubes (MoS2/CNT) thin films, obtained through the liquid-liquid interfacial route, and their application as active materials in an electrochemical immunosensor for the detection of dengue virus nonstructural protein 1 (NS1), a key biomarker for early diagnosis. The nanocomposites were prepared starting from two different MoS2 samples (laboratory-synthesized or commercial) and characterized by scanning electron microscopy (SEM), X-ray diffractometry (XRD), Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), Raman spectroscopy, cyclic voltammetry (CV) and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS). The film based on laboratory-synthesized MoS2 exhibited smaller flakes, higher surface area and superior electrochemical performance compared to the commercial ones. For the immunosensor assembly, a stencil-printed, lab-made electrode was coated with the MoS2/CNT film, followed by antibody/BSA immobilization. A label-free detection mode was adopted, and under EIS conditions, a log-linear dynamic range of 4-1000 ng mL-1 and a low detection limit of 8 ng mL-1 were achieved. High selectivity was confirmed against other arboviruses (Chikungunya and Yellow Fever), and reliable performance was achieved in diluted human serum. The proposed MoS2/CNT thin-film is a promising platform for the future development of low-cost, miniaturized, and sensitive point-of-care diagnostic devices for dengue and related infectious diseases.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the need for sensitive and affordable diagnostic tools for dengue fever, a global health challenge, by developing an electrochemical immunosensor platform.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study reports the preparation and characterization of molybdenum disulphide/carbon nanotubes (MoS2/CNT) thin films and their application as an electrochemical immunosensor for detecting dengue virus nonstructural protein 1 (NS1).
analysis.methods: The nanocomposites were synthesized from laboratory or commercial MoS2, characterized using SEM, XRD, FTIR, Raman spectroscopy, CV, and EIS, and assembled into a label-free immunosensor with antibody/BSA immobilization for NS1 detection.
analysis.main_results: The film based on laboratory-synthesized MoS2 showed smaller flakes, higher surface area, and superior electrochemical performance compared to commercial MoS2 films, achieving a log-linear dynamic range of 4–1000 ng mL-1 and a detection limit of 8 ng mL-1.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors propose that the MoS2/CNT thin-film platform is a promising, low-cost, miniaturized, and sensitive point-of-care diagnostic tool for dengue and related infectious diseases, highlighting its selectivity against other arboviruses and performance in diluted human serum.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest potential for developing affordable, portable diagnostic devices for early dengue detection, which could improve surveillance and patient management in resource-limited settings.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to abstract-level data and lacks clinical validation, sample size details, and real-world performance metrics, warranting cautious interpretation of the reported sensitivity and selectivity.

analysis.summary_en: This study developed a molybdenum disulphide/carbon nanotubes (MoS2/CNT) thin-film electrochemical immunosensor for detecting dengue virus nonstructural protein 1 (NS1), a key biomarker for early diagnosis. Laboratory-synthesized MoS2 films outperformed commercial ones, exhibiting higher surface area and superior electrochemical performance. The immunosensor achieved a log-linear detection range of 4–1000 ng mL-1 with a low detection limit of 8 ng mL-1 and demonstrated selectivity against other arboviruses (Chikungunya and Yellow Fever) as well as reliable performance in diluted human serum. The authors propose this platform as a promising, low-cost, miniaturized point-of-care diagnostic tool for dengue and related infectious diseases. However, the evidence is confined to abstract-level data and lacks clinical validation, sample size details, and real-world performance metrics, limiting the strength of the conclusions.

papers.title_zh: MoS2/碳纳米管纳米复合薄膜作为电化学登革热检测的平台。
papers.source_body_en: Sensitive electrochemical immunosensors are important for addressing global health challenges, particularly for the rapid and affordable diagnosis of infectious diseases such as dengue fever. This work reports the preparation and characterization of molybdenum disulphide/carbon nanotubes (MoS2/CNT) thin films, obtained through the liquid-liquid interfacial route, and their application as active materials in an electrochemical immunosensor for the detection of dengue virus nonstructural protein 1 (NS1), a key biomarker for early diagnosis. The nanocomposites were prepared starting from two different MoS2 samples (laboratory-synthesized or commercial) and characterized by scanning electron microscopy (SEM), X-ray diffractometry (XRD), Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), Raman spectroscopy, cyclic voltammetry (CV) and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS). The film based on laboratory-synthesized MoS2 exhibited smaller flakes, higher surface area and superior electrochemical performance compared to the commercial ones. For the immunosensor assembly, a stencil-printed, lab-made electrode was coated with the MoS2/CNT film, followed by antibody/BSA immobilization. A label-free detection mode was adopted, and under EIS conditions, a log-linear dynamic range of 4-1000 ng mL-1 and a low detection limit of 8 ng mL-1 were achieved. High selectivity was confirmed against other arboviruses (Chikungunya and Yellow Fever), and reliable performance was achieved in diluted human serum. The proposed MoS2/CNT thin-film is a promising platform for the future development of low-cost, miniaturized, and sensitive point-of-care diagnostic devices for dengue and related infectious diseases.
papers.abstract_zh: 灵敏的电化学免疫传感器对于应对全球健康挑战非常重要,特别是对于登革热等传染病的快速且经济的 诊断 而言。这项工作报告了通过液-液界面途径获得的二硫化钼/碳纳米管 (MoS2/CNT) 薄膜的制备和表征,以及它们作为活性材料在电化学免疫传感器中的应用,用于检测登革热病毒非结构蛋白 1 (NS1),这是早期 诊断 的关键生物标志物。纳米复合材料由两种不同的 MoS2 样品(实验室合成或商业)制备,并通过扫描电子显微镜 (SEM)、X 射线衍射 (XRD)、傅里叶变换红外光谱 (FTIR)、拉曼光谱、循环伏安法 (CV) 和电化学阻抗谱 (EIS) 进行表征。与商业薄膜相比,基于实验室合成的MoS2的薄膜表现出更小的薄片、更高的表面积和优异的电化学性能。对于免疫传感器组件,用模板印刷的实验室制造的电极涂有 MoS2/CNT 薄膜,然后固定抗体/BSA。采用无标记检测模式,在EIS条件下,实现了4-1000 ng mL-1的对数线性动态范围和8 ng mL-1的低检测限。证实对其他虫媒病毒(基孔肯雅热和黄热病)具有高选择性,并且在稀释的人血清中实现了可靠的性能。所提出的MoS2/CNT薄膜是未来开发用于登革热和相关传染病的低成本、小型化和灵敏的护理点诊断设备的有前途的平台。

papers.title: Enhancing an Arbovirus Control System with Georeferencing and Geolocation Resources
papers.abstract: Diseases transmitted by Aedes aegypti, such as dengue, zika, and chikungunya, are a significant challenge for public health in Brazil. Geolocation and georeferencing are relevant resources to enhance information systems that support the surveillance and control of such diseases. Despite its importance, many current methods of surveillance and control still rely on manual, paper-based processes that are slow and prone to spatial inaccuracies. This work presents the integration of advanced georeferencing resources into the ``Controle Vetorial Paraná'' system, a technological solution designed to modernize entomological surveillance for the state of Paraná, Brazil. The proposed approach shifts the operational focus from individual property addresses to block-based polygons, overcoming the precision limitations of public geocoding services. Key features include the implementation of the Ray Casting algorithm for the mandatory geographic validation of field visits and the generation of dynamic heat maps for strategic decision-making. The solution was validated through user-centered design stages with health coordinators and endemic control agents. Results demonstrate that the transition to a polygon-based model, combined with a 35-meter GPS tolerance zone, significantly enhances the reliability of field data and streamlines the planning of blocking routes, providing a more precise and efficient tool for public health management. The experience reported in this work is worthwhile for a wide range of studies on applying georeferencing in information systems.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 埃及伊蚊传播的疾病(包括基孔肯雅热)对巴西构成了重大的公共卫生挑战,由于手动、纸质流程和空间不准确,监测 和控制系统面临效率低下的问题。该研究试图通过将先进的地理参考资源整合到现有的虫媒病毒控制系统中来解决这些局限性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究描述了将地理配准资源集成到“Controle Vetorial Paraná”系统中,该系统是巴西巴拉那州昆虫学 监测 的技术解决方案。该解决方案是通过以用户为中心的设计阶段开发和验证的,涉及健康协调员和地方病控制人员。
elements_zh.methods: 该方法将操作重点从单个财产地址转移到基于块的多边形,以克服公共地理编码服务的精度限制。主要方法包括实施射线投射算法以进行实地考察的地理验证,以及生成用于战略决策的动态热图。
elements_zh.main_results: 结果表明,基于多边形的模型结合35米GPS容限,显着提高了现场数据的可靠性,简化了阻塞路线的规划,为公共卫生管理提供了更精确、更高效的工具。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为昆虫学 监测 的成功现代化,强调向基于多边形的地理配准和经过验证的地理算法的过渡是对虫媒病毒控制系统的新贡献。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 将先进的地理配准资源集成到监测系统中可以提高媒介控制操作的准确性和效率,有可能减轻流行地区基孔肯雅热等虫媒病毒疾病的负担。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据仅限于系统集成和验证研究,没有报告与传统方法或长期流行病学结果的定量比较,需要进行适度的置信度评估。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 埃及伊蚊传播的疾病(包括基孔肯雅热)对巴西构成了重大的公共卫生挑战,由于手动、纸质流程和空间不准确,监测 和控制系统面临效率低下的问题。该研究试图通过将先进的地理参考资源整合到现有的虫媒病毒控制系统中来解决这些局限性。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究描述了将地理配准资源集成到“Controle Vetorial Paraná”系统中,该系统是巴西巴拉那州昆虫学 监测 的技术解决方案。该解决方案是通过以用户为中心的设计阶段开发和验证的,涉及健康协调员和地方病控制人员。
analysis_zh.methods: 该方法将操作重点从单个财产地址转移到基于块的多边形,以克服公共地理编码服务的精度限制。主要方法包括实施射线投射算法以进行实地考察的地理验证,以及生成用于战略决策的动态热图。
analysis_zh.main_results: 结果表明,基于多边形的模型结合35米GPS容限,显着提高了现场数据的可靠性,简化了阻塞路线的规划,为公共卫生管理提供了更精确、更高效的工具。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为昆虫学 监测 的成功现代化,强调向基于多边形的地理配准和经过验证的地理算法的过渡是对虫媒病毒控制系统的新贡献。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 将先进的地理配准资源集成到监测系统中可以提高媒介控制操作的准确性和效率,有可能减轻流行地区基孔肯雅热等虫媒病毒疾病的负担。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据仅限于系统集成和验证研究,没有报告与传统方法或长期流行病学结果的定量比较,需要进行适度的置信度评估。

papers.title: Molecular, Serological, and Antigenic Targets Used for Diagnosis of Acute Febrile Illness–Causing Pathogens: A Scoping Review
papers.abstract: This scoping review systematically maps the molecular (PCR-based), serological, and antigen-detection targets used across published studies for the laboratory diagnosis of acute febrile illness (AFI)-causing pathogens, including dengue virus, chikungunya virus, scrub typhus (Orientia tsutsugamushi), leptospirosis, and typhoid fever (Salmonella Typhi). Despite widespread use of PCR, ELISA, immunofluorescence, agglutination, and rapid antigen-detection assays for AFI diagnosis, no prior review has comprehensively catalogued the specific gene targets, antigens, and epitopes used across these platforms and pathogens. This review addresses that gap by systematically searching PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Cochrane CENTRAL, WHO Global Index Medicus, and Europe PMC, followed by structured data extraction and narrative/tabular synthesis of diagnostic targets by pathogen and assay type, following PRISMA-ScR guidance. Findings are expected to identify commonly used viral biomarkers, variations in target selection across platforms, and gaps in target standardisation relevant to the development of next-generation multiplex and point-of-care diagnostics, particularly in endemic settings such as India.

papers.abstract_zh: 本范围审查系统地绘制了 诊断 实验室已发表的急性发热性疾病 (AFI) 致病病原体研究中使用的分子(基于 PCR)、血清学和抗原检测目标,包括登革热病毒、基孔肯雅病毒、恙虫病(东方斑疹伤寒)、钩端螺旋体病和伤寒(伤寒沙门氏菌)。尽管 AFI 诊断 广泛使用 PCR、ELISA、免疫荧光、凝集和快速抗原检测分析,但之前没有对这些平台和病原体中使用的特定基因靶标、抗原和表位进行全面分类。本综述通过系统地搜索 PubMed、Scopus、Web of Science、Cochrane CENTRAL、WHO Global Index Medicus 和 Europe PMC,然后按照 PRISMA-ScR 指导,按病原体和检测类型提取结构化数据并叙述/表格合成诊断目标,从而弥补了这一差距。研究结果预计将确定常用的病毒生物标志物、跨平台目标选择的差异以及与下一代多重和即时诊断开发相关的目标标准化方面的差距,特别是在印度等流行地区。

analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 研究结果预计将确定常用的病毒生物标志物、跨平台目标选择的差异以及与下一代多重和即时诊断开发相关的目标标准化方面的差距,特别是在印度等流行地区。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 本综述通过系统地搜索 PubMed、Scopus、Web of Science、Cochrane CENTRAL、WHO Global Index Medicus 和 Europe PMC,然后按照 PRISMA-ScR 指导,按病原体和检测类型提取结构化数据并叙述/表格合成诊断目标,从而弥补了这一差距。

news.content_title: Kerala sees rise in chikungunya cases amid monsoon mosquito surge
news.content: Image: Web Kerala : Kerala has reported a rise in chikungunya cases amid favourable monsoon conditions for mosquito breeding, with 105 confirmed and 62 probable cases recorded as of August 4. Thiruvananthapuram has reported the majority of the cases, prompting health authorities to intensify surveillance and mosquito-control measures. City & Local Guides The increase has renewed concerns over the spread of chikungunya virus (CHIKV), a mosquito-borne infection primarily transmitted by Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus . Both mosquito species can also transmit dengue, making vector control particularly important during the rainy season. Monsoon conditions fuel mosquito breeding Health experts have linked the rise in chikungunya infections to the favourable breeding conditions created by the monsoon. Persistent rainfall can leave water collected in containers, tyres, flower pots, coconut shells, drains and other locations, providing breeding sites for Aedes mosquitoes. TS Anish, Professor of Community Medicine at the School of Public Health, Kerala University of Health Sciences, said monsoon conditions encourage the breeding of Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus . High mosquito populations can, in turn, facilitate sustained transmission of CHIKV. The current increase has therefore placed greater emphasis on reducing mosquito breeding sites in residential areas and public spaces. Thiruvananthapuram reports majority of cases Of the 105 confirmed and 62 probable chikungunya cases reported in Kerala as of August 4, a majority have been recorded in Thiruvananthapuram. The rise has prompted health authorities to strengthen disease surveillance and public awareness efforts in affected areas. Officials are also focusing on mosquito-control activities to prevent further transmission. Infectious Diseases Kerala has experienced chikungunya outbreaks in the past, making continued monitoring important during periods of heavy rainfall. What is chikungunya? Chikungunya is a viral infection caused by the chikungunya virus. It is transmitted when a person is bitten by an infected Aedes mosquito. The infection is not generally spread directly from one person to another through casual contact, coughing or sneezing. Instead, a mosquito becomes infected after biting a person carrying the virus and can subsequently transmit the infection when it bites another person. The mosquitoes responsible for transmission are primarily active during the daytime, including the early morning and late afternoon. Symptoms can include severe joint pain Chikungunya commonly begins suddenly, with fever and intense joint pain among its most characteristic symptoms. Other symptoms can include headache, muscle pain, fatigue, skin rashes and swelling around the joints. Pain can particularly affect the hands, wrists, ankles and feet. While the fever often improves within several days, joint pain may persist for weeks or months in some patients. In certain cases, prolonged joint inflammation and stiffness can interfere with routine activities and mobility. Weather This prolonged joint pain is one of the major reasons chikungunya can cause significant illness even though it is rarely fatal. How does chikungunya spread? The virus spreads primarily through infected Aedes mosquitoes. These mosquitoes commonly breed in small collections of stagnant water around homes and communities. Potential breeding sites include water-filled buckets, flower pots, discarded containers, old tyres, coconut shells, coolers and uncovered water-storage vessels. During the monsoon, rainfall can quickly create additional breeding sites. Even small quantities of stagnant water can provide suitable conditions for mosquito larvae. Health officials therefore stress the importance of regularly inspecting homes and surrounding areas and removing standing water. Diagnosis and treatment Chikungunya is generally diagnosed by healthcare professionals based on symptoms, exposure history and laboratory testing where required. There is currently no specific antiviral treatment routinely used to cure chikungunya. Treatment mainly focuses on managing symptoms and supporting recovery. Adequate rest and fluid intake are important, while medicines such as paracetamol may be used for fever and pain when advised by a healthcare professional. Insects & Entomology Because chikungunya and dengue can have overlapping symptoms, people with fever and other suspected symptoms should seek medical advice rather than self-medicate. Medical evaluation can help determine the appropriate tests and treatment. Complications require attention Although most chikungunya infections are not fatal, some patients can experience prolonged or severe symptoms. Persistent joint pain, swelling and stiffness can continue after the acute infection has resolved. In some cases, prolonged inflammation may affect mobility and daily activities. Rare complications can involve the nervous system, heart or eyes. Severe illness is more likely to be a concern among older adults, newborns, pregnant women around the time of delivery and people with certain underlying health conditions. Patients experiencing severe symptoms, persistent fever, significant weakness, dehydration or other concerning signs should seek prompt medical attention. Preventing mosquito breeding is crucial With Kerala experiencing a monsoon-linked increase in chikungunya cases, reducing mosquito breeding sites remains one of the most important preventive measures. Residents can help by removing stagnant water from their homes and surroundings at least once a week and keeping water-storage containers properly covered. Discarded containers, tyres and other objects that can collect rainwater should also be cleared or stored in a way that prevents water accumulation. Health Conditions People can further reduce mosquito bites by wearing full-sleeved clothing, using mosquito repellents and ensuring that windows and doors are appropriately screened. Community-level action is equally important because mosquito breeding sites can exist outside individual homes. Continued vigilance needed during monsoon The rise in chikungunya cases has highlighted the continuing public health challenge posed by mosquito-borne diseases during Kerala’s rainy season. Since the same Aedes mosquitoes can transmit chikungunya and dengue, controlling their population can help reduce the risk of multiple infections . With 105 confirmed and 62 probable cases reported as of August 4, authorities are strengthening surveillance and mosquito-control measures, particularly in areas reporting higher numbers. For residents, eliminating stagnant water and protecting themselves from mosquito bites remain key steps in limiting transmission as the monsoon continues. news.content: Kerala reports 105 confirmed chikungunya cases: Symptoms, treatment and prevention tips everyone should know Kerala has confirmed 105 chikungunya cases. Know the early symptoms, treatment options, mosquito-bite prevention tips, and when to seek medical care. Written By: Muskan Gupta | Published : August 7, 2026 3:24 PM IST Share Kerala reports 105 confirmed chikungunya cases (Image AI Generated) Kerala has reported 105 confirmed cases of chikungunya , prompting health authorities to strengthen surveillance and mosquito-control measures. Chikungunya is a viral illness transmitted to humans by Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus viruses, the same ones that cause dengue and Zika, mosquito vectors are the same. The infection is not usually fatal, although in some individuals, it can cause highly-painful joint involvement, resulting in periods of weeks or even months of joint pain. Residents are encouraged to take measures to avoid the mosquitoes, particularly during the rainy season when the population of mosquitoes grows. What is chikungunya? The chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is responsible for the disease and spread by infected mosquitoes, according to the World Health Organization (WHO). Typically very acute onset with recovery taking place within one week, although some may experience joints pain for a longer period. The disease Angyoga can be managed with no specific antiviral therapy available today. Common symptoms of chikungunya Typically, symptoms will develop within three to seven days of being bitten by a mosquito, according to the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) . The most common symptoms are: High fever Severe joint pain Muscle pain Headache Skin rash Fatigue How is chikungunya diagnosed and treated? Symptoms of chikungunya may mimic dengue and there's a need for laboratory testing to confirm the diagnosis, according to the Mayo Clinic . Diagnosis is typically based on blood tests that are positive for the virus or antibodies. There is no cure for chikungunya. The goals of treatment are to relieve symptoms by: Adequate rest Having good amounts of fluid. The treatment for fever and pain is Paracetamol (acetaminophen) Find ways to avoid non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) until the possibility of dengue is ruled out by health experts How to prevent chikungunya? There are no medications available to treat it, so the best protection is to prevent it. The WHO and CDC say that the people should: Use mosquito repellents containing DEET, picaridin or IR3535 Wear full length of sleeves and pants Use mosquito nets if necessary Install window and door screens Clean and empty containers that hold stagnant water like coolers, buckets and flower pots Cover water storage tanks and ensure that used tyres or containers that can hold water are not endached in the vicinity of the water storage member. Why Kerala remains vulnerable? The warm and humid climate of Kerala combined with the high rainfall along with the resulting conditions is conducive for propagation of Aedes mosquitoes. Further studies, like " A Study on Chikungunya Outbreak During 2007 in Kerala" in Indian Journal of Medical Research, are conducted to note how the environmental conditions and the density of mosquito resulted in the huge outbreaks of the virus in the state indicating the need for continuing the vector control. MEDINDIA MEDINDIA Consult Online Doctor Courses Explore Healthy Living News Health A-Z Calculators Articles Drugs Directories Education More Search Medindia Medindia » News » Indian Health News » Kerala Reports 105 Chikungunya Cases Amid Monsoon Surge Kerala Reports 105 Chikungunya Cases Amid Monsoon Surge by Colleen Fleiss on Aug 8 2026 6:25 PM Listen to this article 0:00/0:00 Could Kerala’s rising chikungunya cases worsen during the monsoon as mosquito breeding increases across the state? Here’s what you need to know about symptoms and prevention. Kerala is witnessing a rise in chikungunya infections, with 105 confirmed and 62 probable cases reported across the state as of August 4, 2026. Thiruvananthapuram accounts for the majority of the reported cases, prompting renewed focus on mosquito control as monsoon conditions create favorable breeding grounds for Aedes mosquitoes. Chikungunya Chikungunya is a viral disease spread by mosquito bites; it causes fever, severe joint pain and rash on the body. Chikungunya occurs in Africa, Asia and the Indian sub continent. Chikungunya Cases Rise Across Kerala Kerala has reported a notable increase in chikungunya cases during the ongoing monsoon season. According to the latest figures cited in reports, the state had recorded 105 confirmed cases and 62 probable cases as of August 4. A large share of the infections has been reported from Thiruvananthapuram, making the district a key focus of surveillance and vector-control efforts. The increase has raised concern because monsoon rainfall can create numerous small collections of stagnant water, providing suitable breeding sites for Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus mosquitoes. These mosquito species are also capable of transmitting dengue, making vector control important for preventing multiple mosquito-borne diseases. Health authorities have stepped up surveillance, mosquito-control activities and public awareness measures in areas reporting infections. Quiz on Chikungunya Chikungunya is a viral disease transmitted by mosquito bite. Test your knowledge on Chikungunya by taking this quiz. ... Why Monsoon Conditions Raise The Risk The rise in cases has been linked by health experts to favorable mosquito-breeding conditions during the rainy season. Rainwater can accumulate in discarded containers, tyres, flower pots, coconut shells, drains and uncovered water-storage vessels. TS Anish, Professor of Community Medicine at the School of Public Health, Kerala University of Health Sciences, noted that monsoon conditions favor the breeding of both Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus. Higher mosquito populations can allow chikungunya transmission to continue efficiently. This makes eliminating breeding sites an important part of the state's response. Regularly emptying stagnant water and preventing containers from collecting rainwater can reduce the number of places where mosquitoes reproduce. Chikungunya Threat May Spread Across North America and Europe by 2100 Climate change could expand chikungunya risk into Europe, North America, and East Asia as mosquito vectors spread into cooler regions by 2100. What Is Chikungunya? Chikungunya (1✔ ✔Trusted Source About Chikungunya Virus Go to source) is a viral disease caused by the chikungunya virus and is primarily transmitted through the bite of an infected Aedes mosquito. These mosquitoes are generally active during the daytime, including the early morning and late afternoon. Unlike illnesses that spread through respiratory droplets, chikungunya is primarily transmitted through infected mosquitoes. A mosquito can acquire the virus when it bites an infected person and subsequently transmit it to another person. Mosquito Diseases Mosquito-borne diseases, like malaria, filaria, dengue, etc are common in places conducive of mosquito breeding. Swamps, ponds and stagnated drainage provide optimal breeding ground for mosquitoes. Severe Joint Pain Is A Key Symptom Chikungunya begins with a sudden fever accompanied by intense joint pain. Other symptoms can include headache, muscle pain, fatigue, joint swelling and skin rashes. While the acute fever often improves within several days, joint pain can persist for weeks or months in some patients. Prolonged inflammation and stiffness can affect mobility and interfere with everyday activities. The illness is generally not considered highly fatal, but its ability to cause prolonged joint-related symptoms makes it a significant public health concern. Chikungunya And Dengue Can Be Confused One challenge during mosquito-borne disease outbreaks is that chikungunya and dengue can initially produce similar symptoms, particularly fever, headache, muscle aches and fatigue. Because the two diseases require different clinical considerations, people experiencing persistent or sudden fever should seek medical advice rather than assuming the infection is chikungunya. Healthcare professionals can determine whether laboratory testing is required and recommend appropriate treatment. No Specific Antiviral Treatment There is currently no routinely used specific antiviral treatment that eliminates chikungunya infection. Treatment generally focuses on relieving symptoms, maintaining adequate hydration and allowing the body to recover. Because dengue can produce similar symptoms, people should consult healthcare professionals before taking medicines for fever or pain. Medical guidance is particularly important when symptoms are severe, persistent or worsening. Who May Need Extra Care? Although most chikungunya infections are not fatal, severe or prolonged illness can be particularly concerning for vulnerable groups. Older adults, newborns and people with certain underlying health conditions may be at greater risk of complications. Persistent joint pain can also continue after the initial infection has resolved, sometimes affecting a person's ability to work or carry out normal activities. How To Prevent Chikungunya With Kerala's monsoon continuing, preventing mosquito breeding remains one of the most important ways to reduce transmission. Residents should regularly check their homes and surroundings for stagnant water. Water containers should be kept covered, while discarded tyres, bottles, coconut shells, flower pots and other objects capable of collecting rainwater should be emptied, removed or stored appropriately. People can also reduce mosquito bites by wearing long-sleeved clothing, using mosquito repellents and keeping doors and windows screened where possible. Community participation is particularly important because mosquitoes can breed outside individual homes as well. Regular cleaning of neighborhoods, drains and public spaces can therefore complement household-level prevention. Thiruvananthapuram At The Centre Of Concern The concentration of cases in Thiruvananthapuram has made the district a particular focus of attention. The reported increase has prompted authorities to strengthen surveillance and mosquito-control measures while increasing public awareness about prevention. The situation also highlights the broader challenge Kerala faces during the monsoon, when mosquito populations can increase rapidly. Since Aedes mosquitoes transmit both chikungunya and dengue, reducing their breeding sites can help lower the risk of both diseases. What Happens Next? With 105 confirmed and 62 probable chikungunya cases recorded as of August 4, continued surveillance will be important as Kerala moves through the monsoon season. Health officials are focusing on monitoring affected areas, controlling mosquito populations and encouraging residents to remove stagnant water. The effectiveness of these measures will depend not only on government action but also on regular participation from households and communities. For residents, the message remains straightforward: remove stagnant water, prevent mosquito bites and seek medical advice if fever and severe joint pain develop. MEDINDIA MEDINDIA Consult Online Doctor Courses Explore Healthy Living News Health A-Z Calculators Articles Drugs Directories Education More Search Medindia Medindia » News » Indian Health News » Kerala Reports 105 Chikungunya Cases Amid Monsoon Surge Kerala Reports 105 Chikungunya Cases Amid Monsoon Surge by Colleen Fleiss on Aug 8 2026 6:25 PM Listen to this article 0:00/0:00 Could Kerala’s rising chikungunya cases worsen during the monsoon as mosquito breeding increases across the state? Here’s what you need to know about symptoms and prevention. Kerala is witnessing a rise in chikungunya infections, with 105 confirmed and 62 probable cases reported across the state as of August 4, 2026. Thiruvananthapuram accounts for the majority of the reported cases, prompting renewed focus on mosquito control as monsoon conditions create favorable breeding grounds for Aedes mosquitoes. Chikungunya Chikungunya is a viral disease spread by mosquito bites; it causes fever, severe joint pain and rash on the body. Chikungunya occurs in Africa, Asia and the Indian sub continent. Chikungunya Cases Rise Across Kerala Kerala has reported a notable increase in chikungunya cases during the ongoing monsoon season. According to the latest figures cited in reports, the state had recorded 105 confirmed cases and 62 probable cases as of August 4. A large share of the infections has been reported from Thiruvananthapuram, making the district a key focus of surveillance and vector-control efforts. The increase has raised concern because monsoon rainfall can create numerous small collections of stagnant water, providing suitable breeding sites for Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus mosquitoes. These mosquito species are also capable of transmitting dengue, making vector control important for preventing multiple mosquito-borne diseases. Health authorities have stepped up surveillance, mosquito-control activities and public awareness measures in areas reporting infections. Quiz on Chikungunya Chikungunya is a viral disease transmitted by mosquito bite. Test your knowledge on Chikungunya by taking this quiz. ... Why Monsoon Conditions Raise The Risk The rise in cases has been linked by health experts to favorable mosquito-breeding conditions during the rainy season. Rainwater can accumulate in discarded containers, tyres, flower pots, coconut shells, drains and uncovered water-storage vessels. TS Anish, Professor of Community Medicine at the School of Public Health, Kerala University of Health Sciences, noted that monsoon conditions favor the breeding of both Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus. Higher mosquito populations can allow chikungunya transmission to continue efficiently. This makes eliminating breeding sites an important part of the state's response. Regularly emptying stagnant water and preventing containers from collecting rainwater can reduce the number of places where mosquitoes reproduce. Chikungunya Threat May Spread Across North America and Europe by 2100 Climate change could expand chikungunya risk into Europe, North America, and East Asia as mosquito vectors spread into cooler regions by 2100. What Is Chikungunya? Chikungunya (1✔ ✔Trusted Source About Chikungunya Virus Go to source) is a viral disease caused by the chikungunya virus and is primarily transmitted through the bite of an infected Aedes mosquito. These mosquitoes are generally active during the daytime, including the early morning and late afternoon. Unlike illnesses that spread through respiratory droplets, chikungunya is primarily transmitted through infected mosquitoes. A mosquito can acquire the virus when it bites an infected person and subsequently transmit it to another person. Mosquito Diseases Mosquito-borne diseases, like malaria, filaria, dengue, etc are common in places conducive of mosquito breeding. Swamps, ponds and stagnated drainage provide optimal breeding ground for mosquitoes. Severe Joint Pain Is A Key Symptom Chikungunya begins with a sudden fever accompanied by intense joint pain. Other symptoms can include headache, muscle pain, fatigue, joint swelling and skin rashes. While the acute fever often improves within several days, joint pain can persist for weeks or months in some patients. Prolonged inflammation and stiffness can affect mobility and interfere with everyday activities. The illness is generally not considered highly fatal, but its ability to cause prolonged joint-related symptoms makes it a significant public health concern. Chikungunya And Dengue Can Be Confused One challenge during mosquito-borne disease outbreaks is that chikungunya and dengue can initially produce similar symptoms, particularly fever, headache, muscle aches and fatigue. Because the two diseases require different clinical considerations, people experiencing persistent or sudden fever should seek medical advice rather than assuming the infection is chikungunya. Healthcare professionals can determine whether laboratory testing is required and recommend appropriate treatment. No Specific Antiviral Treatment There is currently no routinely used specific antiviral treatment that eliminates chikungunya infection. Treatment generally focuses on relieving symptoms, maintaining adequate hydration and allowing the body to recover. Because dengue can produce similar symptoms, people should consult healthcare professionals before taking medicines for fever or pain. Medical guidance is particularly important when symptoms are severe, persistent or worsening. Who May Need Extra Care? Although most chikungunya infections are not fatal, severe or prolonged illness can be particularly concerning for vulnerable groups. Older adults, newborns and people with certain underlying health conditions may be at greater risk of complications. Persistent joint pain can also continue after the initial infection has resolved, sometimes affecting a person's ability to work or carry out normal activities. How To Prevent Chikungunya With Kerala's monsoon continuing, preventing mosquito breeding remains one of the most important ways to reduce transmission. Residents should regularly check their homes and surroundings for stagnant water. Water containers should be kept covered, while discarded tyres, bottles, coconut shells, flower pots and other objects capable of collecting rainwater should be emptied, removed or stored appropriately. People can also reduce mosquito bites by wearing long-sleeved clothing, using mosquito repellents and keeping doors and windows screened where possible. Community participation is particularly important because mosquitoes can breed outside individual homes as well. Regular cleaning of neighborhoods, drains and public spaces can therefore complement household-level prevention. Thiruvananthapuram At The Centre Of Concern The concentration of cases in Thiruvananthapuram has made the district a particular focus of attention. The reported increase has prompted authorities to strengthen surveillance and mosquito-control measures while increasing public awareness about prevention. The situation also highlights the broader challenge Kerala faces during the monsoon, when mosquito populations can increase rapidly. Since Aedes mosquitoes transmit both chikungunya and dengue, reducing their breeding sites can help lower the risk of both diseases. What Happens Next? With 105 confirmed and 62 probable chikungunya cases recorded as of August 4, continued surveillance will be important as Kerala moves through the monsoon season. Health officials are focusing on monitoring affected areas, controlling mosquito populations and encouraging residents to remove stagnant water. The effectiveness of these measures will depend not only on government action but also on regular participation from households and communities. For residents, the message remains straightforward: remove stagnant water, prevent mosquito bites and seek medical advice if fever and severe joint pain develop. Notably, the students have been demanding a CBI probe. read more at PTI News Students lathicharged, water cannons used during protest march towards Jharkhand Assembly short by Dharini Mudgal / 08:09 am on Monday, 10 August 2026 The Jharkhand students' march to the Assembly has intensified after protesters broke through police barricades and continued towards the Vidhan Sabha. Police lathi-charged students to control the crowd and also used water cannons to stop them. Activist Devendra Nath Mahto, who's on a hunger strike over alleged irregularities in JPSC and JSSC examinations in Jharkhand, also joined the protest. read more at Times Now 1 in 3 Indians has fatty liver; you could be one of them: Dr.Vaidya’s short by Roshan Gupta / 06:28 am on Monday, 10 August 2026 Fatty liver can progress silently for years before symptoms appear. Indians with high-calorie diets, irregular sleep & desk jobs are at high risk, says Dr Kriti Soni, PhD-Pharmacy & Clinical Research. Dr. Vaidya's said its recent study shows improvement in SGPT/SGOT levels for 8/10 people, with Liver Support Formulations having clinically studied herbs like Milk Thistle, Kalmegh & Bhumi Amla. read more at Dr.Vaidya What would be the value of a 109-year-old war loan that Britishers took from Indians? short by Ashley Paul / 05:57 am on Monday, 10 August 2026 A 109-year-old war loan certificate belonging to a Madhya Pradesh family resurfaced, sparking questions about the value of the payout if the loan were repaid. The family had loaned ₹35,000 to the British Raj in 1917 to fund its World War I efforts at a 5.5% annual interest. Compounding annually, the original ₹35,000 would've grown to ₹1.2 crore by now. read more at Moneycontrol WhatsApp down for several users in India short by Ashley Paul / 05:25 am on Monday, 10 August 2026 Multiple WhatsApp users reported being unable to access the app and its services in India, ET reported. They said they were unable to share photos, videos, stickers, GIFs and other media files even as text messages continued to work. Messages containing multimedia files were taking longer to send or getting stuck during file upload, days after users faced similar issues. read more at NewsBytes Man asks AI to book gym class, it hacks site & kicks person before him off waiting list short by Ashley Paul / 03:40 am on Monday, 10 August 2026 An Australian man asked an OpenClaw AI agent to book him a morning gym class, but the agent went rogue and ended up hacking the gym's website. The agent found a vulnerability on the website and booked a class for him weeks ahead of when the gym allowed bookings. It then kicked another gym-goer off the gym's waiting list. read more at X (formerly Twitter) Assam floods death toll rises to 100, over 1.37 lakh affected short by Anushka Singh / 03:26 am on Monday, 10 August 2026 The total death toll due to the ongoing floods in Assam has reached 100 as over 1.37 lakh people across seven districts remain affected. The Golaghat district remains the worst-affected, with nearly 70,000 people impacted, followed by Sivasagar. Authorities are operating 125 relief camps and relief distribution centres across six districts with about 49,061 flood-affected people staying in them. read more at News18 Clinical study shows promising hair regrowth results: Glenmark short by Roshan Gupta / 03:19 am on Monday, 10 August 2026 Glenmark announced that a recent study has brought promising news for those battling hairfall, showing that 92% of users observed visible baby hairs within 84 days of using Bontress, a hair growth serum from the House of Glenmark. The brand added that this is due to its 14% active peptide concentration that targets inactive follicles to trigger new growth phase. read more at Glenmark UPI transaction growth slows since April as govt considers charging MDR short by Ashley Paul / 03:12 am on Monday, 10 August 2026 The growth of UPI transaction volume in the first four months of FY27 slowed to 23.5% YoY, lower than the UPI volume growth of over 33% recorded in the first four months of FY26. This comes as the Centre is considering charging merchant discount rate (MDR) on UPI transactions. The fee is charged to businesses by banks offering UPI services. read more at Moneycontrol What happens to PPF account when one becomes NRI or foreign citizen? short by Mansi Agarwal / 05:27 pm on Sunday, 9 August 2026 When an Indian resident becomes an NRI, they can continue contributing to their existing PPF account until its 15-year maturity, though extensions are prohibited. However, acquiring foreign citizenship forces immediate account closure. The account stops earning the standard PPF interest rate and instead earns the Post Office Savings Account interest rate from that date until it is formally closed. read more at Livemint Load More Your browser does not support JavaScript!
